bullets.title: Making: Jordan Peele
bullets.note: ([Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/making-jordan-peele/id1171160683?i=1000613493060), [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/2dl6tpa3dDYBzbL51SOXl3?si=A-u1WuH4QRaK2czSoh_rag), [Overcast](https://overcast.fm/+pElY1VGug)) on the [_Making_](https://www.wbez.org/shows/making/71b8de57-b2be-4e03-8481-683258de3ec1) podcast. How are polymaths made? Who was Jordan Peele before [_Key & Peele_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Key_%26_Peele)? This podcast is a hilarious ride that touches on both. Here’s the episode’s description: “[Jordan Peele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Peele) ([@JordanPeele](https://twitter.com/jordanpeele)) is responsible for modern classics in the horror genre, including the films [_Us_](https://www.amazon.com/Us-Lupita-Nyongo/dp/B07PH23CW4), [_Nope_](https://www.amazon.com/Nope-Daniel-Kaluuya/dp/B0B8V3YZ85), and the Oscar-winning [_Get Out_](https://www.amazon.com/Get-Out-Daniel-Kaluuya/dp/B06Y1FYX25). Before all that, he was a self-described nerd. He majored in puppetry in college before dropping out with his friend [Rebecca Drysdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebecca_Drysdale) to pursue a career in comedy. Hear from Drysdale, Peele’s early collaborator [Brendan Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brendan_Hunt) ([@brendanhunting](https://twitter.com/brendanhunting)) \[perhaps best known as the assistant coach in _Ted Lasso_\], and cultural critic [Aisha Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aisha_Harris) ([@craftingmystyle](https://twitter.com/craftingmystyle)) about Jordan Peele’s rise to comedic and horror genius.”

bullets.title: κάλλος
bullets.note: (_kállos_, “beauty”) + [πυγή](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%CF%80%CF%85%CE%B3%CE%AE#Ancient_Greek) (_pugḗ_, “buttocks”). To easily remember it, think of this word: calligraphy, “the art of beautiful writing, elegant penmanship,” 1610s, from Latinized form of Greek _kaligraphia_, from _kállos_ “beauty” + _graphein_ “to write.”

bullets.title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners
bullets.note: ,** created by [Rafał Jaki](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rjaki/) ([@GwentBro](https://twitter.com/GwentBro)) and [Mike Pondsmith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pondsmith), [_Cyberpunk_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberpunk_(role-playing_game)) universe creator. Thanks to Dr. Snapping Turtle for recommending this one. And to cover my ass upfront, a warning: this series is \*very\* intense. To be clear, _Cyberpunk: Edgerunners_ isn’t all blood and guts. There’s some great character development and lots of well-designed plot twists, but… you gotta be able to handle extreme violence. What qualifies as extreme? [Here’s the NSFW trailer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JtqIas3bYhg), and you can judge for yourself. With my renewed interest in making art, it’s been fun to review Japanese while also studying the particular way a lot of anime uses super-detailed backgrounds, extremely high-contrast lighting effects, and so on.
